kjv: therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed
mine: and you, children of Jacob, have not come to an end
note: Hebrew we'attem beney-ya'aqov lo' kelitem is joined by a simple "and"; it may mean "you have not perished" (so KJV, with an added "therefore") or "you have not ceased (from your ways)", leading into 3:7.

kjv: that there may be meat in mine (Yahweh's) house
mine: so that there may be food in My (Yahweh's) house
note: Hebrew teref means food or provisions (the tithes were largely grain, wine and oil); "meat" in 1611 meant food in general.

kjv: that there shall not be room enough to receive it (the blessing)
mine: until there is no more need
note: Hebrew 'ad beli-day means "until there is no lack / without limit"; the KJV's italic supplement "room enough to receive it" gives a picture not in the Hebrew.

kjv: in that day when I (Yahweh) make up my jewels
mine: My treasured possession, on the day that I (Yahweh) act
note: Hebrew segullah is a "treasured possession" (as in Exod 19:5), describing the God-fearers themselves; 'oseh is "act, do" (as in 3:21). The KJV makes "jewels" the object of "make up".

kjv: grow up as calves of the stall
mine: leap like calves from the stall
note: Hebrew pishtem is from push, "frisk, leap, paw the ground" (cf. Jer 50:11; Hab 1:8), describing released calves frolicking rather than growing. (KJV numbers this verse 4:2.)

kjv: the great and dreadful day of the LORD
mine: the great and terrible day of Yahweh
note: Hebrew nora' means "fearsome, awe-inspiring"; modern "dreadful" suggests merely very bad. (KJV 4:5.)

kjv: lest I (Yahweh) come and smite the earth with a curse
mine: so that I (Yahweh) do not come and strike the land with a ban of destruction
note: Hebrew cherem is the "ban" of total destruction (devotion to God), stronger than a curse, and ha'arets here is most naturally the land of Israel. (KJV 4:6.)
